title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when traffic congestion prevented them from reaching charging stations and their batteries depleted. The deployment assumed vehicles would have access to charge during peak traffic events, but the combination of fireworks, major road closures, and high vehicle volumes created conditions the system was not designed to handle. Catching this failure would have required either battery capacity sized for extended gridlock or a protocol to preemptively reposition vehicles away from high-congestion areas during major public events.

The incident exposed a gap between testing conditions and real-world deployment: autonomous vehicles operated in a major city without contingency planning for predictable, recurring traffic surges. The roadside assistance required to tow multiple vehicles suggests the system lacked sufficient situational awareness or decision-making to self-preserve when facing battery depletion in congested areas. It is not established whether Waymo had prior data on Fourth of July traffic patterns in this location that should have prompted different deployment decisions.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Videos verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following a fireworks display near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team towed away the vehicles, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events.

Witnesses reported incidents during the congestion, including one passenger describing a Waymo continuing to drive during fireworks and another person noting frustrated motorists yelling at driverless cars stuck in traffic. The company also reported that one vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries occurred. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the incident with stakeholders to improve traffic management for future events. This marks another challenge for Waymo in San Francisco following a December power outage that also affected its operations.
